title: Random forests capture cancer-specific variation in measured immune-cell response assays
summary: Random-forest models combined receptor–ligand expression measurements to estimate experimentally observed natural-killer-cell responses to tumor samples. Cancer-specific models generalized better within their studied cancer types than a pan-cancer model, whose separate-test AUC fell to 0.638. This is assay-level biological model validation, without established clinical treatment-selection benefit.
ai_technology: Random forests combining receptor–ligand expression features for assay-response classification
organization: University of Science and Technology of China

evidence.tested: The source analyzed 76 distinct NK-cell samples against fourteen ovarian-cancer cell lines, then extended modeling across cancers. Random forests used 70:30 training/test partitions, ten-fold grid-search tuning and twenty random repetitions. A separate pan-cancer test set produced AUC 0.638 and accuracy 63.52%; source-reported breast- and gastric-cancer models reached separate-test AUCs 0.831 and 0.865. The result concerns measured assay response and its cancer-dependent generalization.
evidence.unknown: Random tumor–immune-cell pair partitions do not establish complete donor/cell-line independence; shared entities could affect apparent generalization. Upstream feature screening isolation and supplementary pair-level reconstruction were not verified. Five patient-derived AML samples and one treated patient do not establish prospective clinical efficacy or broad therapy-selection utility. Operational cell preparation, experimental manipulation and treatment protocols were not adjudicated.
evidence.ai_role: Random forests learned nonlinear combinations of expression features linked to measured assay outcomes, enabling the observed distinction between cancer-specific and pan-cancer response prediction. Generic classifier benchmarks alone and untested clinical benefit are not the admitted claim.

source_review.scope: Read actual primary computational model construction/tuning Methods and ovarian/pan-cancer/cancer-specific assay-prediction Results, plus high-level AML validation limitations. Operational biological preparation/manipulation protocols and supplements were not processed or adjudicated. Existing-data assay evaluation is classified retrospectively. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.
